prompt: The development of tourism contributed to English becoming the most prominent lexical in the world. Some people think this will lead to English becoming only language to be spoken globally. Advantages and disadvantages?
essay:
English has become the most common language worldwide due to the increase in international travel. It is claimed that it will eventually become the sole global language. Although this could facilitate communication and reduce the risk of fraud, it could also limit access to historical texts and result in a loss of cultural identity.

One major advantage of English becoming the main language around the world is the ability to communicate with anyone. Since everyone would speak the same language, this would reduce misunderstandings and make interactions easier, particularly when working, living or travelling abroad, as there would be no language barrier. Moreover, being able to understand others regardless of their location or situation could provide greater safety and reduce the risk of being deceived. For instance, due to language barriers, many tourists are scammed when visiting non-English-speaking countries because they may not fully understand the services they are paying for.

On the other hand, eliminating other languages would result in a loss of linguistic resources. Younger generations may no longer be able to understand historical texts, such as literature written in their ancestors’ languages, or fully appreciate what has been passed down to them. This could lead to a loss of cultural identity and traditions, as many of these are closely connected to the original languages of their communities. For example, in Saudi Arabia, people speak several Arabic dialects, each of which reflects the history and heritage of the communities where they developed. These dialects help distinguish people from different regions and create a sense of belonging. Therefore, replacing these languages with English could weaken this cultural connection over time.

In conclusion, having a single global language could facilitate communication and reduce the risk of fraud when travelling abroad. However, this benefit would come at the cost of losing access to historical texts and weakening cultural identity and traditions.
